awd_titl_txt: I-Corps:  Translation potential of a mental health smart neurodiagnostic and neurointervention platform
awd_abstract_narration:
This I-Corps project is based on the development of a mental health smart neurodiagnostic and neurointervention tool. Current diagnostic tools used to assess serious psychiatric disorders face challenges including the clinician's experience, the patient's willingness to disclose symptoms, the time and labor required, behavioral heterogeneity, and expense. This technology is a digital diagnostic and intervention platform that targets neurovascular dysfunction and its related neuromuscular dysfunction, sleep disturbances, impaired autonomous nervous system, and inflammation, which are the main factors in the development and progression of serious psychiatric disorders. The goal is to provide a digital set of quantitative physiological, neural, movement, psychological, and environmental measures of serious mental illness as well as to enhance access for early identification, treatment, and early preventive intervention of serious psychiatric disorders. This technology may reduce the delay in diagnosis of mental illness and improve patient outcomes by treating core psychiatric symptoms, improving neurovascular function and its related conditions.

This I-Corps project utilizes experiential learning coupled with a first-hand investigation of the industry ecosystem to assess the translation potential of a mental health smart neurodiagnostic and neurointervention platform. The platform targets the main neurophysiologic factors in the development and progression of serious mental illness including neurovascular dysfunction and its related neuromuscular dysfunction, sleep disturbances, impaired autonomous nervous system, and inflammation. The solution is based on a model for body-mind biology in development and progression of serious psychiatric disorders. It uses multi-faceted hardware, firmware, and software developed for active and passive data including audio-video of the face; video electroencephalogram (EEG); neurovascular functions; clinical phenotypes of psychiatric disorder; and a custom developed, web-based cloud for body-mind machine learning. In addition, the technology includes a digital reminder intervention and multi-faceted hardware, firmware, and software for augmented reality and neurostimulation intervention for serious mental illness. The digital machine learning algorithms for the identification of serious mental illness, their related psychosomatic disorders, and self-regulation flexibility with neurointerventions may reduce core psychiatric symptoms and treat underlying neurovascular dysfunction and associated psychosomatic disorders at the earliest stages.

This award reflects NSF's statutory mission and has been deemed worthy of support through evaluation using the Foundation's intellectual merit and broader impacts review criteria.

por.por_cntn:
What are the major goals of the project?

The broader impact of this I-Corps project is the development of a) a reliable scalable real-time digital set of quantitative physiological, neural, movement, psychological, and environmental measures of serious mental illness, and b) digital trauma-informed interventions to enhance access for early identification, treatment stratification and early preventive intervention of serious psychiatric disorders through enhancing mental wellbeing and reducing core psychiatric symptoms by improving neurovascular function and its related psychosomatic conditions, that would go undiagnosed and untreated until later in life using the current standard of care tools.

 

* What was accomplished under these goals and objectives (you must provide information for at least one of the 4 categories below

Major Activities:

During customer discovery conducted during our participation in the regional NSF I-Corps program in June 2024 and the national NSF I-Corps program in 2025-2026, interviewing more than 240 pediatrician and psychiatrists was implemented. The majority of pediatricians interviewed reported positive experiences with using technology for assessing serious mental illness (SMI), which assisted them in providing better care to their patients and addressing the current barrier to access to care due to the aforementioned reasons.

 

Specific Objectives:

The customer discover process revealed significant increase in individuals reporting SMI, lack of accurate, scalable diagnostic tool with high sensitivity, shortage of mental health clinicians and low engagement in traditional treatment and being labor intensive, kept providers awake a night, more acute crisis of patients, use of intense outpatient programs, emergency rooms and inpatient services, reduced satisfaction and increased cost.

 

Significant results:

More than 90% of youth visiting pediatrician primary care physician (PCP) reported symptoms of serious mental illness, with 6-month average time between referral to be seen by mental health clinician, gap in communication as not knowing until next visit of what happen to patient, safety concerns, not responding to treatment, and lack of accurate physiologic measure to address treatment resistant patient, frequent crisis intervention, clinician burnout and patient dissatisfaction are major concerns are their major concerns preventing them to sleep at night. Interviewing with multiple Police Office Chiefs, revealed that police response to community and 911 call due to traumatic stress events has been increased by 150% in the last 3 years, impacted personal, social and family life of law enforcers, associated with so many call offs, losing task force, impaired wellbeing and serious mental illness (SMI), impacted job performance and increased suicidality. Furthermore, successful engagement of patients and caregivers was associated with early diagnosis and bouncing back from SMI following a brief intervention. During an interview with Police Wellness Officers and Student Wellness Directors, they found that their initiative of daily 10-minute mindfulness and aerobic exercise improved the cardiovascular and mental wellbeing of their task force, as assessed in their annual checkup.

 

 

Key outcomes or Other achievements:

A new market entrant is needed to streamline the workflow of outpatient mental health practices by eliminating redundant steps, with adaptive individualized treatment stratification and management based on individualized biopsychosocial, physiological, psychiatric, movement, and environmental profiles. Such an individualized, accurate quantitative diagnostic tool, integrating continuity of care with quantitative treatment stratification and interventions, monitoring of response to treatment, can improve patient outcomes and satisfaction, where outpatient mental health practices have been struggling to manage with the current tools and treatment of psychiatric disorders with late-stage presentations.

 

 

 

What opportunities for training and professional development has the project provided?

This project provided evidences regarding a significant gap in access to mental health services, lack of objective diagnostic tools, and low engagement in traditional treatment. The current crisis in mental health care requires a fundamental shift, moving forward with objective and early diagnosis, technology-enabled personalized treatment, and scalable, proactive mental health services.

 

Have the results been disseminated to communities of interest? If so, please provide details.

  • Yes. Findings of this project, revealed a need for an accurate objective scalable tool for diagnosis, monitoring response to treatment and outcome prediction of serious mental illness (SMI), and the need of a strength-based brief neurointervention for SMI
